To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most severe constraints on four-quark and four-lepton contact interactions arise at the high energy colliders, not from atomic parity violation; and that the atomic parity violation measurements provide the best tests of compositness for contact interactions which preserve approximate global symmetrues other than parity.
the most severe constraints on compositeness arise from the high energy experiments and that these constraints are not affected by atomic parity violation.
the most severe constraints on four-fermions compositeness interactions come from the high-energy collider experiments at LHC, Tevatron, and HERA.

the study of composite quarks, leptons, and the Higgs boson.
the development of a new class of composite materials that are capable of being formed into complex structures and that have the ability to sense the environment and respond to external stimuli.
the development of new materials for high temperature applications and with the development of novel processing methods for these materials.

the evidence of a possible violation of parity is not yet conclusive.
the atomic parity violation measurements are consistent with the Standard Model and that there is no evidence for new physics in atomic parity violation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the most stringent limits on contact terms in the quark-lepton sector come from high energy collider experiments, and the most severe constraints on contact terms in other sectors are provided by atomic parity violation experiments.
we have found a way to use the atomic parity violation experiment as a tool to search for new physics at high energy.
the most stringent tests of composite quark and lepton interactions will be provided by high energy experiments at LEP, HERA, the Tevatron and future colliders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the most stringent tests of composite quarks or composite leptons come from the high-energy experiments, not from low-energy atomic experiments.
atomic physics can provide stringent constraints on new physics at the electroweak scale.
atomic parity violation is not the most sensitive test of new physics.
